reasoning: The baseline Random Forest achieved 95.11% CV accuracy with standard preprocessing. Logistic Regression (iter01_c1) improved this to 97.02% by adding StandardScaler and using balanced class weights, indicating the data benefits from linear separation when features are normalized. The previous Gradient Boosting attempt (iter01_c3) underperformed RF at 95.12%, likely due to aggressive regularization or insufficient depth. To explore complementary strategies: 1) Test a more complex tree ensemble with higher capacity (Random Forest with max_depth=10) to see if it can beat the baseline without overfitting, given the small dataset size. 2) Refine the successful Logistic Regression by increasing C (weaker regularization) to test if the model is currently too conservative on this balanced-ish dataset. 3) Introduce a Stacking approach combining the best-performing base models (RF and LR) with a meta-learner, as ensembles often handle non-linear interactions better than single models in tabular data.
